newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil sheds gains, tracks NYMEX to end down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil sheds gains, tracks NYMEX to end down.

text.p: IPE gas oil retraced gains to close lower on Tuesday after a downside move by NYMEX products futures and the release of European stocks data pushed the market off earlier highs, brokers said.
Dec gas oil closed $2.75 a tonne lower at $212.75, having touched a session high of $218.50. The front month contango closed $1 wider at $2 a tonne.
"When NYMEX heat came off we just couldn't stay up there," said one broker.
NYMEX heating oil came under pressure from warmer U.S. weather forecasts, brokers said.
The National Weather Services six to 10 day outlook released on Monday forecast above normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.
The release of European Union stock data showing a heavy build in distillate stocks helped to push gas oil off highs, brokers said.
Middle distillate stocks in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose by 2.55 million barrels or 0.9 percent in November to 295.73 million barrels, the Euroilstock foundation said on Tuesday.
Distillate stocks were 770,000 barrels higher than at the end of November 1995, wiping out the year-on-year shortfall that has persisted for most of the year.
Jan Brent was trading 46 cents down at $23.64 a barrel at 1752 GMT, off the session low of $23.58.
The contract breezed through support at $23.77 as NYMEX crude fell heavily, triggering technical selling stops.
Traders said that delays to Iraqi crude exports failed to lend support to the market. A Turkish oil official said that no Iraqi oil had arrived at the Ceyhan export terminal on Tuesday.
